title: PR-001 verification gate registry v1
description: Validates gate_registry_v1.json: the frozen VG-A..VG-E gate table. Exactly five entries, one per gate, each with a frozen feeder RT and exactly one machine receipt path. The registry is configuration only: it MUST NOT carry any mutable execution status. additionalProperties:false plus the forbiddenEntryKeys list below structurally prevent a status/conclusion/verdict field from creeping back in.

downstream_only_ids.description: IDs that are strictly downstream of every VG and must never appear as a VG input.

consumer_relation_model.description: Prose statement freezing the TWO separate consumer relations over VG-A..VG-E: `consumers` (direct RT consumers, value space {RT-024, RT-026}) and `release_gate_consumers` (release-gate consumers, value space {G3, G4, G5, G6}). Earlier revisions carried only the first while the plan asserted the second, which read as a contradiction; both are now explicit and neither is derivable from the other.

release_gate_registry_ref.description: Pointer to the authority for the release-gate side of the second relation. The inverse of release_gate_consumers here must equal consumes_verification_gates there.

status_resolution_rule.description: Prose statement that runtime status comes only from receipt_path existence plus the receipt's own status/conclusion.

prerequisite_rank_rule.description: Prose statement of the exact rank constraints from which every gate's allowed_prerequisite_ids is derived (RT rank capped at feeder_rt, strictly earlier VGs only, only already-upstream release gates), plus the ref_id uniqueness requirement.

consumers.description: RELATION 1 - DIRECT RT CONSUMERS. The RT delivery packages whose own implementation reads this VG receipt JSON as an input. Value space is exactly {RT-024, RT-026}; a release gate must NEVER be added here. This is not the release-gate consumption relation, which lives in release_gate_consumers.

release_gate_consumers.description: RELATION 2 - RELEASE-GATE CONSUMERS. The release gates that must cite this VG receipt inside their frozen prerequisite set. Value space is exactly {G3, G4, G5, G6}; an RT must NEVER be added here. Frozen as VG-A -> [G3, G6], VG-B -> [G6], VG-C -> [G4, G6], VG-D -> [G5, G6], VG-E -> [G6], which must be the exact inverse of consumes_verification_gates in release_gate_registry_v1.json. G6 appears for every gate because final acceptance re-binds all five; G1 and G2 appear for none because no VG exists before RT-015; G7 appears for none because an authorization consumes no verification evidence beyond G6.

allowed_prerequisite_ids.description: Frozen exhaustive allowlist for this gate's receipt prerequisite_refs[].ref_id. Derived from the rank rule at prerequisite_rank_rule; any ref_id outside this set is a forward reference and must fail closed. G6, G7 and RT-026 are excluded by pattern; the gate's own id and every later VG are excluded by the rank rule.

static_note.description: Static rule/scope statement only. Must never describe a run outcome.

semanticRules: The registry is frozen configuration: neither the top level nor any gate entry may carry a mutable execution status (see forbiddenEntryKeys).
Runtime status is derived only from receipt_path existence and the status/conclusion inside that receipt.
gate_id values are unique and cover exactly {VG-A, VG-B, VG-C, VG-D, VG-E}.
feeder_rt values are unique; the frozen mapping is VG-A=RT-015, VG-B=RT-018, VG-C=RT-021, VG-D=RT-023, VG-E=RT-025.
receipt_path is unique per gate and its VG-x segment matches gate_id.
No gate may list G6, G7 or RT-026 as a producer or as a prerequisite input.

`consumers` is RELATION 1, DIRECT RT CONSUMERS, restricted to RT-024 / RT-026. `release_gate_consumers` is RELATION 2, RELEASE-GATE CONSUMERS, restricted to G3 / G4 / G5 / G6. The two relations are disjoint in value space and neither is derivable from the other; a release gate must never appear in `consumers` and an RT must never appear in `release_gate_consumers`.

release_gate_consumers is frozen as VG-A -> [G3, G6], VG-B -> [G6], VG-C -> [G4, G6], VG-D -> [G5, G6], VG-E -> [G6], and must be the EXACT inverse of consumes_verification_gates in release_gate_registry_v1.json. The two files are cross-checked in both directions, so a one-sided edit is a detectable contradiction rather than a silent divergence.

Being a release-gate consumer of VG-x and being in VG-x's allowed_prerequisite_ids are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE for the same G: a gate that consumes VG-x cannot also be upstream of it. G3, G4 and G5 therefore appear in release_gate_consumers of VG-A, VG-C and VG-D respectively and are absent from those same gates' allowed_prerequisite_ids. G6 consumes every VG and appears in no allowlist at all.
allowed_prerequisite_ids must never contain the gate's own gate_id, nor any VG later than it in the frozen wave order VG-A < VG-B < VG-C < VG-D < VG-E.
allowed_prerequisite_ids must never contain an RT whose ordinal exceeds that gate's feeder_rt.
allowed_prerequisite_ids must never contain a release gate that consumes this gate: G3 consumes VG-A, G4 consumes VG-C, G5 consumes VG-D.
allowed_prerequisite_ids is monotonically non-decreasing along VG-A -> VG-E: each gate's allowlist is a superset of the previous gate's allowlist plus that previous gate id.
